issues.legal_issue: A beneficiary who owns property that a will intends to dispose of must elect between retaining that property and taking a benefit under the will.
material_facts: A registered settlement transferred property to the beneficiary, and the settlement was acted upon through mutations and the beneficiary obtained title and possession.
A later will stated that prior settlements and wills were cancelled and that the later will alone would govern the disposition of the estate.

The will gave the beneficiary several properties that had been settled on other family members and left the residue to another beneficiary, without specifically identifying the property previously settled on the claimant.
The claimant asserted a right to the settled property while also claiming the properties given to him under the will.
issues.conclusion: The will showed that the testator intended to dispose of the property previously settled on the claimant. The claimant was therefore put to election and could not claim that property if he wished to take the benefit provided for him under the will.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 180 of the Indian Succession Act, 1925, where a will purports to dispose of property that belongs to another person and gives that person a benefit, that person must elect either to confirm the disposition or to dissent and give up the benefits under the will. The provision does not apply the English principle of compensation. A testator is generally presumed to intend to dispose only of the testator’s own property, so general words will not usually include property over which the testator had no power of disposition; however, an intention to include that property may be shown expressly or by necessary implication from the will read as a whole. The Court referred to Miller v. Thurgood, Whitley v. Whitley, Re Allen’s Estate, Prescott v. Allen and Beaumont, and Re Booker, Booker v. Booker.

rule.if: testamentary_election_dispute and beneficiary_owns_property and will_grants_benefit and will_clearly_disposes_of_beneficiary_property and beneficiary_takes_benefit

predicates.testamentary_election_dispute: The proceeding concerns a claim to property and benefits arising from a will.
predicates.beneficiary_owns_property: The person given a benefit under the will already owns property that the will purports to dispose of.
predicates.will_grants_benefit: The will provides a benefit to the person who owns the property.
predicates.will_clearly_disposes_of_beneficiary_pro: The will, read as a whole, shows expressly or by necessary implication that the testator intended to dispose of the beneficiary’s property.
predicates.beneficiary_takes_benefit: The beneficiary takes a benefit provided under the will.

issues.definition: When a will proceeding involves a beneficiary who owns property the will clearly purports to dispose of, and the beneficiary takes a benefit under that will, the beneficiary cannot claim the owned property while retaining the will benefit.
